hls_winter_cover_pct.source: data/processed/field_year.parquet winter_cover (notes/fields.md), focus-area fields, crop years 2021-2026
hls_winter_cover_pct.note: lower bound on cover-crop use, not an adoption estimate

headline.shown: equal-weight mixture (levels[].avoided), with trials only (levels[].trials_only.avoided) alongside
headline.why: The mixture keeps both lines of evidence in the range. The river-model half has no tested skill (bare-soil features barely change leave-one-year-out error), so trials-only is shown next to it as the trial-anchored figure.

method: What-if replay on the MEASURED river. X = X% of all upstream corn/soy acres add cover, beyond the ~17% already covered statewide (X = 25 takes coverage from ~17% to ~42%). Each day's nitrate is cut by a share taken half from Iowa trial results (INRS 2024: cereal rye cuts drainage nitrate 28% on average, SD 26%; applied Oct-Jul, scaled by the row-crop share of river nitrate) and half from a river-model sensitivity (bare-soil features add no tested skill) to less bare soil (Oct 15-May 31). The headline is this 50/50 mixture, shown next to 'trials only'. The river-model half is not validated: its bare-soil features improve leave-one-year-out error by only 0.002-0.005 (ln units), yet at 25% it cuts the annual load by 8.7% at the Des Moines River and 2.0% at the Raccoon (trials: 4.8%). The mixture's plant-day and cost results lean on the river-model half: in 2025 at 25% it avoids 17 plant days against 10 for trials only (mixture 16). Read 'trials only' as the conservative, trial-anchored figure. Plant and ban days use proxy rules fitted to 2025 and tested on 2026; in 2025 and 2026 a plant day counts only if the plant really ran that day. Adopters are assumed to be typical fields; the river may take more than one season to respond (legacy nitrate). Satellite (HLS, 30 m) detects winter cover on only 0.8-4.2% of fields a year, against ~17% statewide adoption: it sees only cover that has grown enough by late fall or early spring, so it is a lower bound (many covers are drilled late or stay small).

method_detail.quantiles: p50 = median; lo/hi = 10th/90th percentile of draws (8 in 10)
method_detail.impact_basis: relative change applied to the OBSERVED daily concentration, C'(t) = C_obs(t) x (1 - D(t)); flow unchanged; counts on measured days only; loads use measured flow x gap-filled concentration
method_detail.avoided: computed inside each draw (baseline minus scenario), then summarised
method_detail.plant_day_rule: 2025 and 2026 (reported run dates, facts plant_days_<year>): a plant day is a day the proxy says 'on' AND the real plant ran, so avoided plant days are real run days the scenario switches off. Aug-Nov 2026 proxy days (no reported run) never count. 2016-2024: no run dates, proxy only. plant_days_proxy keeps the proxy-only count as a diagnostic.
method_detail.trials_only: levels[].trials_only.avoided: same engine with every draw on the trial path (a), for every year and level
method_detail.hls_cover_detection: Satellite (HLS, 30 m) detects winter cover on only 0.8-4.2% of fields a year, against ~17% statewide adoption: it sees only cover that has grown enough by late fall or early spring, so it is a lower bound (many covers are drilled late or stay small).

path_a_trial.formula: daily cut on Oct-Jul days = X * e * s; annual load cut dL = X * e * s * w

e.dist: normal truncated to [0,1], location solved so the mean equals the stated efficiency

s.source: model/out/basin_index_check.json rowcrop_share_of_river_load (notes/fields_model.md: 1 - INRS point share x row-crop share of land load)

w.definition: share of the calendar year's measured (gap-filled) load passing Jan-Jul and Oct-Dec, i.e. the fall-to-July drainage window cover crops act on

path_b_learned.definition: relative change of the simulated median concentration when the causal bare share is cut by X (relative) on Oct 15-May 31, all cover features recomputed (model/river.py perturb_cover + predict)
path_b_learned.spread: bootstrap refits over training years (sensitivity.json, 5-95%, split-normal) + SD of the median/p10/p90 models' responses
path_b_learned.caveat: Historical bare-share variation is overwhelmingly seasonal (bare in winter/spring, green in summer) and its year-to-year differences are driven by weather (planting/green-up timing, harvest date), not by cover-crop adoption, which stayed at single-digit % of cropland. The model therefore never saw a watershed with much more winter living cover, so the learned sensitivity is weakly identified: the monotone constraint fixes its sign (less bare soil never raises nitrate), but its size is uncertain and a 50% cut takes winter bare share far outside the training range, where trees extrapolate flat (
path_b_learned.skill: bare-soil features add no tested skill: leave-one-year-out ln-RMSE gain raccoon 0.0052, desmoines 0.0023 (sensitivity.json diagnostics)
path_b_learned.note: the bootstrap spread does not capture the identification problem (historic cover variation is seasonal), so inverse-variance weights favour this path; path-only results are reported for comparison

method_detail.blend: equal-weight mixture: 50% of Monte Carlo draws use the trial-prior path, 50% the learned-model path (so the range spans both lines of evidence); inverse-variance weights are reported only as a diagnostic because the learned path's bootstrap spread omits its identification problem

caveats: Legacy nitrate: soils and groundwater hold years of nitrate, so a change on fields takes more than one season to show in the river; results describe the effect once it has developed, replayed on that year's weather.
Current adoption is already ~17% of Iowa corn+soy acres (statewide, secondary); X is a share of ALL upstream corn/soy acres ADDED on top (X = 25: ~17% -> ~42%).

Satellite (HLS, 30 m) detects winter cover on only 0.8-4.2% of fields a year, against ~17% statewide adoption: it sees only cover that has grown enough by late fall or early spring, so it is a lower bound (many covers are drilled late or stay small).
The river-model half of the mixture has no tested skill (bare-soil features barely change leave-one-year-out error); 'trials only' is shown alongside.
Plant days avoided count only days the plant really ran (2025, 2026 reported run dates).
Adopters are assumed to be typical fields; targeting leaky, tile-drained fields would do more, poor establishment less.
Trial efficiencies are mean drainage-concentration cuts with a large SD (28 +/- 26%); the river-model response is weakly identified (historic cover variation is mostly seasonal).
Plant and ban days come from proxy rules (the utility's rules are not public); 2026 test: see thresholds.calibration.
Cost avoided is operating cost only; capital is not avoided in the short run.
lb N kept = nitrate that would have reached the two gauges; on-farm retention is larger (in-stream removal not counted).
2026 is a partial year (data through 2026-11-13); 2026 nitrate data are partly provisional.
